 On Bukayo Saka going off injured...

 'You start airing it in public and it doesn't end well for anyone' published at 23:11 BST 23:11 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Stephen Warnock 
Former Liverpool defender on MOTD: UEFA Champions League 
 I think there will be ex-players now from Manchester United saying, 'why are you letting this get out, this should be a collective in the changing room where we come together'. Whether you like the manager or not, you've got to come together and say 'OK how do we correct this'. 
 Senior players go to the manager and say 'listen we didn't agree with the tactics, we didn't think we got it right, how do we go about this, how do we move forward' because you start airing it in public and it doesn't end well for anyone.

 'I don't get impression they are going to rip up template' published at 23:09 BST 23:09 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter in Como 
 It's not easy to see someone like Antonio Conte going into Manchester United and living at peace with the ownership. I can't see that because he has never done it anywhere else, and that's not really worked at Man Utd when you look at people like Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal to an extent, but I'm not sure that Manchester United are set up in that way and I don't get the sense that they are going to rip up the template of what they had. 
 I think the problem for Manchester United is that again, in the summer of 2024 they had a good think about Erik ten Hag to be their manager, they gave him some money to spend in the transfer window and sacked him in October.
 The following year last summer they did something similar with Ruben Amorim and then sacked him in January, but many people thought he could have gone a long time before that. And now, they are in a similar position again. I don't get the impression that they are going to rip up the template. But you have to look back over three years and think are the decisions being made the right decisions, and it doesn't look like it.

 'Man Utd need to decide who will be in charge against Bournemouth' published at 23:01 BST 23:01 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter in Como 
 I think Michael Carrick is almost struggling for answers at the moment. 
 I don't know if it's the angriest he's been, I think he's been quite forceful in his pre-match press conferences with the media lately, I have been on the wrong end of that. He does it in quite a calm way, not like Sir Alex Ferguson but I think he's trying to be on the front foot and today is just a really bad day.
 I immediately thought when he went to the fans, acknowledging them like he did, hands in the air, four or five times, was a bit like Ole Gunnar Solskjær who did something very similar after a 4-1 defeat to Watford. He admitted that he knew at half-time in that game that his time at Manchester United would come to an end.
 Now, United have flown straight back after the game so presumably there will be a lot of thought going on on that plane as it heads back to Manchester. But, first of all, Manchester United need to decide who will be in charge of that game against Bournemouth on Sunday, and Bournemouth aren't in brilliant form, they won the last game, but they have only won one game this season, and they are playing tomorrow night so Manchester United should be really looking to win that game even though Bournemouth have a fantastic record at Old Trafford. 
 Do Manchester United give Michael Carrick that game and see from there, or do they think we need to make a change?

 'Arsenal will miss Saka but have players who can step up' published at 22:42 BST 22:42 BST 
 FT: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal 
 Nedum Onuoha 
Former Man City defender on MOTD: UEFA Champions League 
 As far as the game goes, getting a result like that against Bayern, with Arsenal probably believing they could go on and get the win at the end, is very impressive.
 The only negative is seeing one of their star players, Saka, having to pull up with an injury early in the first half. He was lying on the floor with his hand up and he knew he was in a bit of trouble, so now the concern will be how long he is out for.
 (Saka's absence) It's not necessarily something that means the team will struggle heavily but there is a reason why he is regarded as one of the best players in this Arsenal team and is seen as being important for them. They will still be hoping he isn't out for so long.
 This is one of the reasons their squad has been built the way it has been and I think Madueke and Eze did well on the wings today after Saka came off (Madueke had started on the left but switched to the right with Eze coming on to the left).
 In terms of options, at this moment in time for Arsenal, it is not going to be an issue... they will miss the star power that he has, they still have plenty of other wide players who can step up and do the job while they wait for him to come back.

 By Alex Howell Football reporter at the Allianz Arena Declan Rice scored a late equaliser as Arsenal and Bayern Munich played out an entertaining draw in the league phase of the Champions League in a game where Bukayo Saka limped off with injury. 
 Saka went down after just 10 minutes with a suspected thigh problem, after he attempted to play a pass without anyone around him.
 Eberechi Eze replaced Saka and scored the opening goal of the game in the 35th minute, after he latched on to an excellent pass by Martin Odegaard, with the video assistant referee needing to intervene after the England international was initially flagged offside.
 But Bayern Munich were behind for just 10 minutes, with Harry Kane picking the ball up in midfield and splitting the Arsenal backline with a pinpoint pass for Alphonso Davies to finish.
 Kane, who had produced a number of eye-catching passes during the match, then put Bayern in front from the penalty spot.
 The England captain's shot struck Jurrien Timber's hand inside the area and Kane sent David Raya the wrong way from 12 yards as he looked to have completed the turnaround. 
 Bayern piled the pressure on to Arsenal as they looked for a third goal but the Gunners held firm before Rice exchanged passes with substitute Viktor Gyokeres and drilled a low shot into the bottom corner to level the game. 
 The Gunners pushed for a winner and Jurrien Timber forced Manuel Neuer into an acrobatic stop before full-time. 
 Figure caption, 'This could be a real problem for Arsenal tonight and going forward'
 What did you learn from Arsenal’s display? 
 Another all-action performance from Rice - Arsenal player ratings 
 Starting XI 
 David Raya: A very good save down low from a Serge Gnabry shot in the first half and an even better one from Dayot Upamecano in the second. His long-range passing was a big weapon for Arsenal in this match. 7 
 Jurrien Timber: Looked like he had regained some of his old sharpness. Some good moments going forward but got caught for one of the Bayern goals. 6 
 Ezri Konsa: The centre-back was given the tough task of sticking close to Harry Kane and had to follow the striker all over the pitch. A decent performance but also booked for a late tackle. 7 
 Gabriel Magalhaes: A solid game from Gabriel but part of a backline that conceded twice. 6 
 Riccardo Calafiori: The left-back is usually known for his attacking ability but he put in a good defensive display even though Arsenal conceded twice. 7 
 Declan Rice: The usual all-action display from Rice and he capped the performance with an excellent equaliser. 8 
 Bruno Guimaraes: The midfielder still looks like he is getting up to speed after joining the club. Some nice moments on the ball and almost scored with a header. 6 
 Martin Odegaard: An excellent pass for the opening goal and looked bright all evening. 7 
 Bukayo Saka: Started brightly but had to be withdrawn after just 10 minutes as he picked up what looked like a thigh injury, going down when nobody was near him as he attempted a pass. 5 
 Noni Madueke: Started on the left but switched to the right and was direct all night. Lots of effort and bright moments but nothing to show for it. 6 
 Kai Havertz: Some nice moments of link play but not enough of an attacking threat. 6 
 Subs: 
 Eberechi Eze (on 10, Saka): Scored the opening goal with a great finish low into the corner. A much-needed goal. 8 
 Viktor Gyokeres (on 68, Havertz): Came on and exchanged passes with Rice for the equaliser. 7 
 Myles Lewis-Skelly (on 69, Guimaraes): A big game to come on in from the bench and did well. 6 
 Mikel Merino (on 85, Odegaard): Introduced as Arsenal looked for a winner. 6 
 Subs not used: Meslier, Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Dowman.
